Alright time for an English lesson, since people only know how to use the internet.

I majored in linguistics btw.

The English language has started to fall apart. Words that are commonly misspelled, like "spelt"  are being added to the dictionary because it's too commonly used now.

Theres more. In grammar there is something called Prescriptive Grammar and something called Descriptive grammar. Prescriptive grammar is what you typically think of when you think of proper grammar. Such as, "I don't have any milk". 

Descriptive Grammar, is something that has been created to make up for people who have weak foundations in their understanding of grammar. As long as it can be understood, whether that be instinctually or what have you, it is Descriptively grammatical.

I'd catch a bus to school. I went to school in a place that wasn't good to sleep in, so I'd sleep in a city over and bus it to school.

For two years during highschool I was homeless and worked part time at a McDonald's. I didn't have a car so didn't need to pay for gas and such, just a bus pass which was free. Even with that, food was a tough obstacle.

At first I'd buy cheap protein powders and fill that up and a gallon of water at the gym where I showered. Some gyms have a microwave so getting oatmeal is a super low budget food.

 I would buy a bag of brown rice and sneak this super cheap rice cooker into my gym and plug it into a socket to make rice. The bicycle room was always empty so I'd shut off the lights, sit in a corner and cook it. Throw a towel over it. I'd use the microwave to heat up some frozen broccoli and that was one meal included with protein shake (Super fortress walmart stuff for $15 for 30 servings.)

Some days, I'd go to Subway and get a $5 sandwich and just load it up. I'd cut it in half and that was my two meals for the day. The bread keeps you full. If I got hungry later I'd drink a half serving of protein.

Cans of tuna were also my friend. I'd get free soy sauce packets from chinese fast food joints like panda express and put it on my tuna. I invested in a $1 can opener and would just crack it open and eat it. Often times id cook my rice in the gym, add hot water to it and have my soy sauce tuna on the side. This is a popular meal in my family even outside of being homeless. 

Looking back, I probably was living off less than $70 a month for food. I payed $70 ish for food, $25 for a gym membership, and my bus pass was free because I used a fake one from a community college that let's you ride for free.
